### Motivation

Issue #576 records two quota sinks. Tasks covering the same mathematics were
dispatched weeks apart, so several open pull requests declare results `main`
already contains and the overlap surfaced only at review or merge (212, 296,
398, 488, 539, 289, 274 were the day's examples). And on 2026-09-17 a helper
and the main session repaired PR 577 at the same time.

This PR builds the model-free tooling of parts A, B and C of the issue. Part D
(just-in-time update with approval carry) is not implemented here.

### Description

- `scripts/dup_scan.py` — the scanner. It indexes a git ref's Lean declarations
  by parsing blobs through `git show` (no checkout, no build) and matches a
  query three ways: `fqn` (same fully qualified name), `statement` (same
  statement after a cheap normalisation — comments stripped, proof cut at the
  top-level `:=`/`by`/`where`, binder names renamed positionally, whitespace
  collapsed) and `short` (same last name component inside the `MIPStarRE`
  namespace). It sits beside `check_duplicate_private_helpers.py`, the existing
  audit that compares Lean declarations the same textual way.
- `local/bin/dup_check.py` — the workflow front end.
  - `check` takes `--name`, a blueprint node label (`--node`, its `\lean{}`
    names) or a branch/PR head (`--branch`/`--pr`, its declarations new against
    the merge base). Exit 0 clean, 3 duplicates printed as `file:line`, 2 usage
    or environment error; `--json` is the machine form.
  - `sweep` does the same for every open PR and writes the `audits/` report.
  - `claim` / `claims-check` / `claims-release` / `claims-list` maintain
    `local/registry/declaration-claims.jsonl`, an append-only registry binding
    declaration names to the issue producing them. A claim is refused when
    another issue's open claim holds the name or when `main` already declares
    it; `--force` records it anyway and still exits 3, so an accepted overlap
    stays in the log.
  - `predispatch` is the one-call form `dispatch.sh` uses.
- `local/bin/dispatch.sh` runs the check for the `prover`, `mathfix` and
  `simplifier` roles before the session starts. Advisory by default:
  `MIPSTARRE_DUP_CHECK=fatal` refuses the dispatch, `off` skips it, and a
  non-numeric `--issue` scope word is skipped with that explanation.
- `local/bin/claim.sh` brings the meta session's atomic worker-claim list into
  the repository. The file format it writes is unchanged; only its location is
  now overridable (`MIPSTARRE_CLAIM_FILE`) so it can be unit tested.
- `scripts/blueprint_lean_sync.collect_file_lean_decls` gains an optional
  `text=` argument so a ref can be parsed without a checkout. Behaviour is
  unchanged when the argument is absent.
- `local/protocols/issues-prs.md` section 7 and a dated `EVOLUTION.md` entry
  record that native delegates and Opus helpers run the check before starting
  or repairing proof work, and that issue creation records the claim.

No tool calls a model. The only network read anywhere is the list of open PRs
in `sweep`; the matching itself is local git.

Two notes for the reviewer. The scanner lives under `scripts/` because that is
where the repository's other Lean-source audits live, and the split also keeps
this commit at 663 of the pre-commit hook's 1000-line workflow-layer budget; no
override was used. And the guards are advisory by construction — a `statement`
or `short` match is a prompt to read both declarations, never a verdict about
the mathematics. No Lean statement, definition or gate is touched by this PR.

### Sweep report

`audits/2026-09-17_superseded-pr-sweep.md` is the run over the open pull
requests at the time of writing: **69 examined, 38 with at least one new
declaration `github/main` already contains, 34 of those matched by fully
qualified name**. The report carries its own limitations section — notably that
a stacked PR whose base has since merged shows its parent's declarations as new
against its own merge base, so part of a large count is stack staleness rather
than a second proof, and that an overlap between two *open* PRs is invisible to
the sweep (the claims registry is what covers that case). PRs 212 and 274 are
not flagged: their new declaration names and statements are genuinely absent
from `main`, so whatever was duplicated in them is not a main-branch collision.

### Testing

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p "test_*.py"` — 733 tests,
  all passing (685 before this change; 48 new across `test_dup_check.py`,

record.after:
### Motivation

Issue #576 calls for checks that avoid duplicate proof work and overlapping
worker assignments. This PR implements parts A, B and C. Part D, the documented
just-in-time update and approval-carry workflow, remains open.

### Description

- Add a model-free Lean declaration scanner and `local/bin/dup_check.py` for
  matching declaration names, normalized statements, blueprint labels and
  branch contributions against a local Git reference. Matches are advisory
  prompts for mathematical inspection. Exit 0 means no match, 3 means matches,
  4 means the reference could not be read and the check was skipped, and 2
  means a usage or environment error.
- Add an append-only declaration-claims registry and a repository copy of the
  atomic worker-claim script. Declaration claims and worker reservations remain
  distinct records.
- Add an advisory pre-dispatch check and document duplicate-work checks in
  section 7 of the issue/PR protocol. Existing section 6 remains unchanged.
- Include a dated sweep of 69 open PRs: 38 have declarations matched on main,
  including 34 with fully qualified name matches. The report distinguishes
  matched declarations from match counts and documents stale-stack limits.
- Reuse the existing Lean parser through an optional text input. No Lean
  statement, blueprint completeness claim or merge gate changes.

### Testing

- All nine exact-head local CI contexts succeeded on `d418467d`.
- The fresh independent reviewer ran all 55 tests in the four new test
  modules successfully using synthetic repositories, with no network or model
  calls and a clean worktree before and after.
- The reviewer checked the missing-reference exit-4 behavior, existing
  duplicate exit-3 behavior, protocol numbering, sweep counts and front matter.
  The sweep was checked for internal consistency and one sampled match; the
  reviewer did not rerun the full sweep or full test suite.

---
Addresses #576
